# Model routing

<!-- Generated by `py -3 tools/test_docs.py --render-routing` from `settings/model-routing.json` and `settings/model-evidence.json`. Edit the JSON, never this page. -->

Which model, at which effort, for which kind of work, and the evidence behind each choice. Setup reads `settings/model-routing.json`, drops every model your organisation does not allow and keeps the first allowed entry of each row's preference order; SessionStart shows the first five rows, which are the most common task shapes (the table is in that order). Spawn the persona named in the row (see `docs/HOW-WE-WORK.md`).

How to read the evidence: `vendor` = published by the model maker; `independent` = measured by a third party; `kit-bench` = a re-run with this kit's neutral task packs; `internal-run` = a small run by the kit's authors, shown by direction and month only; internal rows never rank a routing pick. Tier R0 = one party measured it, R1 = one independent replication, R2 = two or more. A row with only R0 evidence is a starting point: run your own task pack before relying on it. Dates, exact values and sample sizes are in `settings/model-evidence.json`.

## Routing table

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| R-breadth | BREADTH: search and fetch fan-outs, collecting (even for a decision), and browser, command-line or tool-server loops | general-purpose | claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-opus-5-5 (high) | claude-haiku-5-5: its best tool-automation score sits below the mid-tier's lowest effort, and at low effort in long agent prompts it skips searches and checks<br>claude-fable-5-1: costs several times as much for a lower tool-automation score | E7, E8, E9, E13, O2, O4 |
| R-read | READ: extract, classify, summarise or digest text or files that are handed over, in a few tool calls | scout | claude-haiku-5-5 (high) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (high) | claude-haiku-5-5: never for facts from memory, tool loops, code, ops, security, regulated work, final deliverables or gates<br>claude-haiku-5-5 at xhigh or max: xhigh can end a chat turn with no visible text and max spends several times the output tokens of high | E10, E11, E12, E13, E14, E15, O1, O3 |
| R-build | BUILD: a code, configuration or infrastructure change with no obvious shape, an irreversible change, or work a worker already failed | flagship | claude-opus-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: far behind on hard repository tasks<br>any model at max effort: no gain over xhigh for the top tier and a higher bill | E1, E4, E5, E6 |
| R-gate | GATE: final pass, verification, judging or tie-break on finished work | blue-verify | claude-opus-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: its vendor documents reporting a change as done without running a check, and it over-refused most in the vendor's audit | E24, E18, E25, E14 |
| R-research | RESEARCH: multi-source synthesis and web research that needs judgment | researcher | claude-opus-5-5 (high) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: factual recall far below the larger models<br>claude-fable-5-1: about twice the cost for a slightly lower web-research score, so use it only when asked for by name | E16, E17, E15 |
| R-ops | OPS: anything run on a machine, such as shell work, runbooks, container and service changes, and diagnostics | ops-runner | claude-opus-5-5 (high) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: far below the larger models on terminal-task benchmarks<br>any model at max effort: no better than xhigh on terminal tasks for a higher bill | E1, E2, E28 |
| R-deliverable | DELIVERABLE: a final document, deck or spreadsheet for a person or a third party (internal drafts: researcher) | flagship | claude-opus-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: fine for an internal first draft, but it trails the larger models on every deliverable benchmark, so it never writes the final version | E21, E22, E23 |
| R-security | SECURITY: review code, configuration or an environment for vulnerabilities | security-auditor | claude-opus-5-5 (high) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: its cyber safeguards trigger on security work and it has no fallback, so the task stalls or is refused | E14, E24, E27 |
| R-regulated | REGULATED: legal, tax, medical or compliance work; cite primary sources, then pass the result to blue-verify | flagship | claude-opus-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) | claude-haiku-5-5: last on every legal, tax and medical benchmark it is listed on<br>claude-fable-5-1: leads the max-only legal and tax benchmarks at several times the cost, so offer it and never route to it by default | E19, E20, E16 |
| R-red | RED: adversarial review or pre-mortem on a different model from the builder; attacks, never gates | red-team | claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-opus-5-5 (high) | - | E24, E25 |
| R-green | GREEN: an independent alternative design or rebuild from a different model than the builder | green-team | claude-sonnet-5-5 (xhigh) > claude-opus-5-5 (high) | - | E26, E25, E22 |

| Id | Kind | Tier | Source | Finding |

| E1 | independent | R0 | Artificial Analysis: Terminal-Bench 4.0 on the per-effort model pages (artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-opus-5-5-high and sibling pages) | On a terminal-task benchmark the mid-tier at xhigh and the top tier at high are within a point of each other at similar cost, the top tier scores no higher at max than at xhigh, and the small model's best setting stays below the mid-tier's high setting. |

| O1 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: persona configuration check | Headless runs of every persona confirmed that each ran on its pinned model, that the small-model alias resolved to the current small model, and that a reader persona set to high effort used its high thinking band instead of falling through to a higher level. Easy probes did not separate the larger models' effort settings, so their persona efforts stay as configured. |
| O2 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: cost breakdown of real subagent sessions | Re-pricing real subagent sessions at published list prices showed that cache writes and cache reads made up most of each persona's cost and that most agent turns carried prompts above the long-prompt threshold, so model price times context size, not effort, was the main cost driver. |
| O3 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: small-model reader cost on agent work | Re-pricing the same measured agent tokens at published list prices, with the long-prompt tier applied per turn, put the small model well below the mid-tier's cost on long agent work and lower still on short workflow tasks. |
| O4 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: effort step on a collecting worker | Raising a mid-tier collecting worker from high to xhigh effort on a repository search loop raised the cost of the run, in line with the published price slope for the same step. |
| O5 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: small-model effort probe | In one internal probe on the small model, raising effort from low to high improved adherence to a length instruction and turning thinking off lowered it; a closing line restating the rules did not help; output tokens and the share of replies with thinking rose with effort. |
| O7 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: blind replay of past subagent prompts | Two blind labelers sorting past subagent prompts by task type agreed on most of them; the main disagreement was collecting work done for a decision, and the most common misroute to the top-tier builder was an already-planned code slice. |
| O8 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: reader against mid-tier on classification | On a classification pass over past prompts the reader persona agreed with a top-tier labeler as often as the mid-tier in one repeat and less often in the other, inside its own repeat-to-repeat variation, at a lower cost; in one repeat it over-applied a judgment label. |
| O9 | internal-run | R0 | claude-workbench authors: output tokens by effort on small tasks | On small agentic and logic tasks every effort level passed on each model tested, so those tasks priced effort and could not rank it: output tokens, thinking included, rose at nearly every step, the priciest tier's step from high to xhigh cost far more than the top tier's, and a subagent ran at its own model's saved effort level rather than the main session's. |
